
DEPENDENCIES
Show all dependency relationships for a work unit (blocks, blockedBy, dependsOn, relatesTo)

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to quickly view all dependency relationships for a specific work unit. Shows which work units it blocks, is blocked by, depends on, and relates to. Essential for understanding work unit relationships and planning implementation order.

PREREQUISITES
  • spec/work-units.json exists with work units

USAGE
  fspec dependencies <work-unit-id> [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <work-unit-id> (required)
    Work unit ID to show dependencies for

OPTIONS
  --graph
    Display dependencies as graph visualization (shows dependency tree)

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Quick Dependency Check
    Example: # Before starting work, check what blocks this work unit
fspec dependencies UI-001

# Output shows:
#   Blocked by: AUTH-001, API-001
#
# Decision: Wait for AUTH-001 and API-001 to complete
    undefined

  • Understanding Impact
    Example: # Check what will be unblocked after completing this work
fspec dependencies AUTH-001

# Output shows:
#   Blocks: AUTH-002, AUTH-003, UI-001
#
# Completing AUTH-001 will unblock 3 work units
    undefined

  • Dependency Tree Visualization
    Example: # View full dependency tree
fspec dependencies AUTH-001 --graph

# Shows cascading dependencies
    undefined

  • Integration with add-dependency
    Example: # Add dependency
fspec add-dependency UI-001 AUTH-001

# Verify it was added
fspec dependencies UI-001
# Output: Depends on: AUTH-001
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Create work units → 2. Add dependencies with add-dependency command → 3. View relationships: fspec dependencies <id> → 4. Plan implementation order based on dependencies

EXAMPLES
  1. Show dependencies for work unit with no relationships
  $ fspec dependencies MCP-001
  Dependencies for MCP-001:

  2. Show dependencies for work unit with multiple relationships
  $ fspec dependencies MCP-004
  Dependencies for MCP-004:
  Depends on: MCP-001, MCP-002
  Blocks: MCP-005
  Related to: DOC-MCP-004

  3. Show all dependency types
  $ fspec dependencies AUTH-001
  Dependencies for AUTH-001:
  Blocks: AUTH-002, AUTH-003
  Blocked by: INFRA-001
  Depends on: SCHEMA-001
  Related to: DOC-001

  4. Show dependencies as graph visualization
  $ fspec dependencies AUTH-001 --graph
  AUTH-001
  blocks → AUTH-002
    blocks → AUTH-004
  blocks → AUTH-003

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: Work unit 'INVALID-999' does not exist
    Fix: Verify work unit ID exists. Run: fspec list-work-units

Note: This error includes AI-friendly system-reminder with suggestions.

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec add-dependency - Add dependency relationships between work units
  fspec remove-dependency - Remove dependency relationships
  fspec query-bottlenecks - Find critical path blockers
  fspec suggest-dependencies - Auto-suggest dependencies based on patterns
  fspec export-dependencies - Export dependency graph (JSON/Mermaid)
  fspec show-work-unit - Show complete work unit details (includes dependencies)

NOTES
  • Simplified Command (BUG-019):
  •   - This command was simplified from multi-action to single-purpose
  •   - Old: fspec dependencies <action> <work-unit-id>
  •   - New: fspec dependencies <work-unit-id>
  •   - Other actions now use dedicated commands (add-dependency, remove-dependency, etc.)
  • 
  • Relationship types displayed:
  •   blocks: Work units blocked by this work unit
  •   blockedBy: Work units blocking this work unit
  •   dependsOn: Soft dependencies (ordering hints)
  •   relatesTo: Related work units (no blocking)
  • 
  • Error handling:
  •   - Non-existent work units show AI-friendly system-reminder
  •   - System-reminder includes troubleshooting steps
  •   - Wrapped for visibility in Claude Code
  • 
  • For comprehensive dependency management:
  •   - add-dependency: Create relationships
  •   - remove-dependency: Delete relationships
  •   - clear-dependencies: Remove all relationships
  •   - export-dependencies: Visualize full graph
  •   - query-bottlenecks: Find critical path issues
